fuel.note: Pumps are those drawn on the open map within the search radius of the road. A pump missing from the map is missing here, so each gap is a worst case.

rules.title: Sandakphu: motorcycles stopped at Manebhanjan
rules.detail: Motorcycles are turned back at the Manebhanjan check post since April 2018, after a forest officer's notice. A blog updated September 2026 says this still holds. Notice text not found.
rules.set_by: Divisional Forest Officer, Darjeeling Wildlife Division, West Bengal Forest Department

source.title: Tour of Sandakphu and Phalut by Car

history.change: Notice by the Divisional Forest Officer barred motorcycles from the Sandakphu road; reported 11 April 2018.

source.title: Bikers Will Not be Allowed in Sandakphu from Now Onwards: Notice by Divisional Forest Officer

history.change: Blog states that no motorcycles or private vehicles run inside the park as of 2026.

source.title: A COMPLETE Sandakphu Travel Guide for all Trekkers and Tourists

rules.title: Sandakphu: only association vehicles run the road
rules.detail: Visitors change at Manebhanjan to vehicles of the local Land Rover owners' association. A travel site says private cars need its consent, rarely given. No government order found.
rules.set_by: Singalila Land Rover Owners' Welfare Association, in practice

source.title: Tour of Sandakphu and Phalut by Car

rules.title: Singalila National Park: entry permit at Manebhanjan
rules.detail: Issued at the Forest Department office in Manebhanjan against photo identity; foreign citizens show a passport. A blog says a guide is compulsory inside the park.

source.title: Tour of Sandakphu and Phalut by Car

rules.title: Singalila National Park: closed in the monsoon
rules.detail: Closed to visitors from 16 June to 15 September every year. One travel site gives 15 June as the first day.

rules.title: Sandakphu: police health advisory for visitors
rules.detail: Darjeeling Police host a health advisory for Sandakphu visitors on their website. The file could not be opened, so its contents are not recorded.

source.title: Health advisory for tourists visiting Sandakphu

season.note: The Sandakphu road lies inside Singalila National Park, which shuts every monsoon on fixed dates; no year-by-year dates were found.

hazards.title: Hill roads cut by rain, October 2025
hazards.detail: Rain on 4 and 5 October 2025 brought down the Dudhia bridge and damaged Rohini Road. A temporary bridge opened on 27 October 2025.

source.title: Dudhia Bridge to reopen on Monday; Rohini Slip repair underway

hazards.title: Bypass roads can be closed or restricted
hazards.detail: After the October 2025 damage one bypass was shut following a fatal accident and another was kept for emergency and school vehicles only.

source.title: Dudhia Bridge to reopen on Monday; Rohini Slip repair underway

hazards.title: Landslides on National Highway 10 into Sikkim
hazards.detail: The road along the Teesta was shut for six days in August 2025 after it collapsed near 9th Mile. Repeated slides slowed repairs.

source.title: NH-10 reopens after six days of landslide disruption in Sikkim and Kalimpong

gaps: The text and number of the April 2018 forest notice barring motorcycles from the Sandakphu road were not found; it is known only from a blog and a travel site.
No official West Bengal Forest Department page found for Singalila entry rules, fees or closure dates.
Darjeeling Police health advisory for Sandakphu returned an access error (HTTP 403) and was not read.
No source found stating whether Indian or foreign citizens need any permit for Darjeeling and Kalimpong towns.
Usual number of days for the whole Siliguri, Darjeeling, Kalimpong loop not sourced; the figure given covers only the Sandakphu leg.
Highway number for the Kalimpong leg not sourced beyond National Highway 10 along the Teesta.
Entry fee amounts come only from a blog and are left out.
No year-by-year opening or closing dates found for the Sandakphu road.
Some stretch distances are doubtful. The open map may not know the road riders use, so the routing service went the long way round.
